screening_results.reason: This is an fMRI study where human participants performed a risky decision-making task (CUPS gambling task) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted. The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky vs non-risky trials, main effects of decision and feedback) and parametric modulation analyses (risk and reward), with group-level whole-brain results (FLAME, thresholded maps) presented in figures and tables. Thus it meets I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Recommendation: INCLUDE for meta-analysis of fMRI studies of reward-related cue-reactivity in the context of task-evoked whole-brain activation.

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning in adolescents and adults, so it meets I4 (task-based risky/uncertain decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrasts: PFB vs NFB-Stay/NFB-Switch etc.). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (ACC, VS, vmPFC) and does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates/results from whole-brain statistics. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Additionally, the study does not address the review’s focus on drug/natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants using the risky-gains decision-making task (risk task), with explicit within-task contrasts (risky vs safe) and between-group comparisons. The analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level (linear mixed effects, voxel-wise thresholds and cluster correction reported), and results are reported as whole-brain clusters/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4–I7 are satisfied.

The study reports fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (an ambiguous/risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts for decision/outcome phases (advantageous vs. disadvantageous choices; wins vs. losses), and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses in addition to ROI analyses. Whole-brain between- and within-group results are described (posterior cingulate/precuneus, MPFC, etc.), meeting the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results are available in the text/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not address the review objective (meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although this is an empirical fMRI study with participants performing a risky decision-making task (I4 met) and the authors ran whole-brain group-level analyses and reported whole-brain results/figures (I6 and I7 met), it does not report any within-task or between-task contrast directly related to risk (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk) required by I5. The primary reported fMRI contrasts concern conditioned-stimulus (relief vs. fear) cue responses and model-based ROI correlations, and no unmasked whole-brain risky>safe (or analogous) task contrast is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study collected fMRI during a risky gamble decision-making task (Experiment 3) using visual conditioned cues (fractals) and reports group-level, second-level voxelwise analyses. The authors tested within-task contrasts that index risky versus safe decisions within an interaction (decision × conditioned stimulus) and report activation coordinates (left amygdala) from the group analysis; they also provide whole-brain exploratory maps/coordinates (supplementary). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Note: the study uses monetary conditioned cues rather than drug cues, but it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I4–I7 as specified.

Exclusion decision rationale: This paper is an empirical fMRI study of risky and strategic decision-making and meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky/strategic decision tasks), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky/uncertain choices, e.g., B-choice > A-choice and task contrasts across lotteries/stag-hunt/entry), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with FWE correction), and I7 (reporting of whole-brain results with peak MNI coordinates and text/figures). However, it does NOT address the meta-analysis review objective (fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Because the study topic (decision-making/strategic uncertainty) does not match the review objective, it is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses (variance comparisons within preselected SPL/IPL ROIs) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or standard within-task/between-task activation contrasts. Exclusion ID E3 applies. Inclusion: I4 is satisfied (human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task on ambiguous faces). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no reported within-task or between-task activation contrast maps related to perceptual decision-making) and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps; results are ROI-based variance tests). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, DOI). Therefore the study fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and is excluded.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts including risky > sure and sure > risky), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported with whole-brain FWE correction), I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion IDs not met: none. Primary reason for exclusion: although the study satisfies the listed inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug- and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (no cue-reactivity, drug/natural reward, or visual cue paradigm). Therefore it is not relevant to the stated meta-analysis objective and is excluded on those grounds. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorization of multi-element visual arrays), with parametric contrasts of perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (mean- and variance-related uncertainty; e.g., proximity-to-bound, variability) reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (SPM8), with peaks/clusters and tables/figures described in the text (cluster-corrected results and coordinates). Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported via tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making (random-dot motion) and a rule-based decision task (Sudoku), meeting I4. It includes within-task contrasts and parametric regressors related to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., task > control, hard/low-coherence effects, uncertainty-level regressions), meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME; FDR/FWE thresholds) with whole-brain statistical maps described in text and figures, meeting I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a multi-step gambling task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (quota-severity and strategy-optimization contrasts tied to risky vs. EV-based choices) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates). Thus all inclusion criteria for risky/decision-making fMRI studies are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (visual motion direction discrimination). It includes within-task parametric contrasts modulated by motion coherence (i.e., perceptual difficulty; equivalent to “low coherence > high coherence” type effects) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level permutation t-tests, cluster-level FWE correction) with maps and peak coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Although the overall meta-analysis objective mentions reward cue-reactivity, the provided inclusion criteria focus on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making: criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a monetary/probabilistic reward task that manipulates uncertainty (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and reward magnitude. The authors report within-task contrasts explicitly modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., high uncertainty [50%] vs low/no uncertainty [100%]) and other contrasts (magnitude, value, prediction error). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level ANOVAs with FDR/FWE correction and results reported in tables/figures/text. Full article includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I4 (human fMRI task involving risk/ambiguity), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI during the cups risky decision-making task (I4). It includes within-task contrasts related to risk and outcomes (e.g., risky > safe; win > loss) and between-group contrasts (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with GRF-corrected thresholds and two-sample t-tests (I6), and whole-brain results are described in text, figures and tables (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and original empirical task-based fMRI data are reported. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria; include in meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain risky decision-making fMRI data.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential virtual foraging task that entails probabilistic (risky) decisions between foraging and waiting. The paper reports within-task, task-evoked contrasts and parametric modulators tied to risk-related decision variables (e.g., probability of foraging success, value differences of foraging vs. waiting, uncertainties, discrepancies). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and peak MNI coordinates, fulfilling the requirement that whole-brain results be available (coordinates and figures/tables provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets the review inclusion criteria: (I4) participants underwent fMRI while performing a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game); (I5) contrasts of interest include risky vs safe decisions (go vs stop) and peer/parent contrasts; (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-FWE corrected whole-brain results and NeuroVault repository); (I7) whole-brain results are described in text/figures and made available. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity-only analyses (E4) — although PPI is reported, whole-brain task activation maps are also provided — not only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is an empirical fMRI study (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (n=24) that collected whole-brain task-evoked BOLD data while participants performed a financial decision-making task under risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators directly related to risky decision-making (probability weighting, weighted lottery value, sure-win magnitude) and contrasts (MESSAGE vs NO MESSAGE; follow vs ignore advice) tied to risk-related processing. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (t-maps, cluster thresholds, tables/figures). Results are described with figures and coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this study used fMRI during a probabilistic two-armed bandit decision-making task (meets I4) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (meets I6 and I7), it does not report at least one within-task or between-task contrast explicitly related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, risky > safe). The fMRI analyses focus on parametric modulators of expected value (Q) at choice and reward/RPE at outcome, but do not present contrasts that map onto the risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts required by I5. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I6) and presents whole-brain results clearly in text/figures (I7), it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards and therefore does not meet the review’s topical scope. Additionally, it does not provide an explicit within-task whole-brain contrast framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I4 and I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a risk-taking decision-making task (anticipatory risky choices), with within-task conditions including high-risk and low-risk, reward and loss (satisfying I4/I5). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with familywise-error whole-brain correction and whole-brain clusters (satisfying I6/I7). Results include whole-brain contrasts (group, group×valence, feedback main effects) and coordinates/ROI follow-ups; it does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the article meets all specified inclusion criteria for whole-brain risky decision-making fMRI studies and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study is an instrumental probabilistic reward- and punishment-based reinforcement learning task in depressed and control participants. It does include group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (satisfying I6) and reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (satisfying I7). However, it does not meet the primary task-domain inclusion criteria: the task is a reinforcement learning/associative learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (criteria I4 and I5). The reported contrasts are reward vs neutral, punishment vs neutral, and prediction-error regressors, not contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), analyses are task-evoked (not resting-state/connectivity-only), and the paper is an empirical study. Full text appears complete. Therefore I exclude because I4 and I5 are not met.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study of perceptual decision-making and confidence (random-dot motion task) with whole-brain group-level activation maps. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli: no drug or natural reward cue exposure, no cue-reactivity paradigm, and no contrasts targeting reward-cue reactivity. Regarding the inclusion criteria: it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). It does not satisfy I5 because the reported contrasts focus on confidence-related parametric modulation and EEG-informed regressors rather than perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence) or a perceptual task>control contrast relevant for perceptual-DM inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for not addressing the review objective and for failing to provide the required perceptual-contrast (I5).

This is an fMRI study of perceptual trajectory prediction and computational/modeling of dynamic vs statistical predictions. Although it meets several methodological inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4: fMRI during a perceptual decision task; I5: task-related within-task parametric contrasts; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses; I7: whole-brain results reported), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The experimental stimuli and aims concern trajectory extrapolation and computational model specialization, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to address the review objective/relevant population/phenomenon of interest.

The study meets the review inclusion criteria: (1) It performed fMRI while participants completed a risky decision task (laboratory and smartphone risky decision tasks) satisfying I4. (2) Neural analyses included within-task task-related contrasts/regressors tied to risky decision-making (expected value and reward prediction error correlates linked to choices/outcomes), satisfying I5. (3) Group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported/displayed (main effects images at uncorrected P<.001 and reported activations including medial PFC), indicating whole-brain analyses were performed, satisfying I6. (4) Whole-brain results are presented as figures/images (acceptable per I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task that probes decision-making under uncertainty (probabilistic/ambiguous feedback). The authors report within-task contrasts (lose-shift vs other feedback conditions) that index decision-related behavioral adjustment and present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses and reported cluster peaks). Whole-brain activation maps and peaks are described in the text and figures/SI. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. Thus it meets criteria for an fMRI task probing ambiguous/risky decision-making, provides relevant within-task contrasts, and reports whole-brain group-level results.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk (risky > safe; punishment feedback > risky) and additional contrasts examining effects of punishment on subsequent choices. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are described with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster correction (P < 0.001, cluster-level), and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical restriction).

This fMRI study involved human participants performing decision-making tasks under uncertainty (diagnosis/prescription vs naming), manipulating diagnosticity (high vs low) to index ambiguity/uncertainty, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to diagnostic uncertainty/diagnosticity (e.g., foreperiod > high-diagnosticity first stimulus; epoch and diagnosticity ANOVAs), meeting I5. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with random-effects inference and FWE correction and peak MNI coordinates reported, satisfying I6 and I7. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. It reports an fMRI reversal learning task and analyses of prediction-error (PE) signals in the ventral striatum and their relation to life stress and fluid intelligence. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analysis was performed) and I7 (whole-brain results referenced/shown in supplementary materials). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 and I5 — the task is a reinforcement/reversal learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task with contrasts such as “risky > safe” or “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, and no such risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts are reported. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED for not meeting the domain-specific inclusion criteria of the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This paper investigates novelty-driven exploration and reinforcement learning in a four-armed bandit task using neutral landscape images, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making/novelty bonuses), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet, but the study fails to address the review’s topical objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). Exclusion criteria applied: none of E3–E6. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with a motivation manipulation (monetary incentive) and includes appropriate within-task contrasts (motivated > neutral; stimulus+decision > implicit baseline). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and provides results in the text and ROI-corrected follow-ups. It is an empirical, complete full text with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects).

Although the study meets the provided task-based fMRI inclusion criteria (it used the BART risky decision-making task in human participants and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The meta-analysis objective requires studies of visual cue-reactivity; this study examines decision-making/risk processing after wins/losses rather than neural responses to visual reward-related cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts / parametric modulation of risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: study does not assess visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (so does not address the review objective). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Does not address the review objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Although this is an fMRI study of risky decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps and contrasts (skewed vs symmetric; positive vs negative skew) and reports group-level voxelwise results, it investigates monetary gambles rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not conceptually eligible for a meta-analysis focused on reward cue-reactivity. Full text is complete.

The study does not address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and does not include the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and I5 (no within-task contrasts corresponding to risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or perceptual hard>easy; reported contrasts are gain/loss/omission vs neutral and PE parametric modulators). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria and does not address the specific review objective.

Although this study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for the review (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task with within-task contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paradigm manipulated monetary motivation in an animal-detection task rather than presenting drug or natural reward cues (e.g., food, drug-related images) for cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered (whole-brain results reported, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Therefore I exclude the study for not meeting the review’s topical objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity).

While this full-text reports an fMRI perceptual decision-making task with appropriate within-task contrasts (high vs low coherence), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis, and reported coordinates, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making: high>low and low>high coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Because the study does not investigate reward-related cue-reactivity (topic mismatch with review objective), it is excluded. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study includes a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) and a passive picture-viewing task of appetitive food images. It reports a within-task contrast of reward>punishment from the reversal learning paradigm and positive>neutral for picture viewing, satisfying the requirement for a contrast related to decision-making/reward. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed using FLAME with nonparametric permutation testing and threshold-free cluster enhancement; group-level contrasts and peak coordinates are reported, indicating whole-brain task-evoked maps were produced. Results are presented with coordinates and corrected statistics. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (50/50 monetary gambles) with in-scanner task performance — satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts (novel vs familiar prime) that are directly related to modulation of subsequent risky choices and perform a regression linking this contrast to percent risky choices across subjects (a within-task, task-related contrast) — meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses with coordinates for hippocampus and putamen), satisfying I6 and acceptable under I7. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes full methods, results, and discussion, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches) with visual reward-predictive cues and natural reward (juice). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses correlating trial-by-trial model regressors (predicted reward V(t) and reward prediction error δ(t)) with BOLD signals, including FDR-corrected maps and peak MNI coordinates. The study manipulates stimulus discriminability (high vs low contrast) and examines its effect on brain responses, satisfying perceptual-decision contrasts related to stimulus difficulty/discriminability. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric effects tied to perceptual discriminability), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making paradigm (Colorado Balloon Game), fulfilling I4. It includes within-task contrasts isolating decision-related activity (Decision Trial – Directed Trial) and separates deliberations preceding risky vs. cautious responses, fulfilling I5. Analyses are reported as group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and Monte Carlo estimation; results are described in tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and presents whole-brain task activation contrasts (not only between-group contrasts without task effects), so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article should be included for the meta-analysis.

Although this study is an fMRI investigation in healthy adults and meets the methodological inclusion criteria for decision-making tasks (I4, I5) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I6, I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paradigm is a probabilistic reasoning/uncertainty (beads/JTC) task rather than a cue-reactivity task involving drug or natural reward cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: the study does not investigate reward-related cue-reactivity (topic mismatch). Full text appears complete.

Although the study does include an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (auditory/vocal emotions) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses and contrasts, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with peak coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Primary reason for exclusion: study population/task/stimuli do not involve reward-related cue-reactivity nor visual stimuli required by the review objective, so it is not relevant to the review.

Although the study includes an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an ambiguous perceptual/valence decision (intermediate dissonance > consonance) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates/figures (I4, I5, I6, I7 are satisfied), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This study uses auditory (musical) stimuli and investigates emotional valence and uncertainty, not reward-related cue reactivity or visual cue processing. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore it must be excluded because it does not match the review topic (reward-related, visual cue-reactivity).

This study meets all specified inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies. I4: Subjects underwent fMRI while performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). I5: The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (DecBa vs DirBa; decision-period contrasts; win vs loss contrasts). I6: Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed (SPM5 ANCOVA; cluster-level FWE/AlphaSim corrections). I7: Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures with coordinates and detailed description in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not only between-group contrasts without unmasked task effects; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a decision-making task (a modified ultimatum game) in which proposers choose between fair and selfish offers that carry varying risk of rejection. The contrasts reported (e.g., choosing slightly selfish > fair; fair > selfish; high stakes > low stakes) are within-task decision-making contrasts reflecting choices under risk/uncertainty. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM with reported cluster-level results and MNI coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI of risky/decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of decision-making on abstract value word pairs in managers vs. non-managers, not a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual reward cues. It does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required (I4 and I5 not met). The paper does report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results and lists coordinates (so I6 and I7 are satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded because it does not address the review objective and fails to meet I4 and I5.

Although this fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (Social Analogue Risk Task) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (parametric modulation during cash-out decisions) with coordinates and cluster-corrected maps, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The stimuli are dynamically changing facial expressions (social cues), not drug or natural reward cues, so the paper is not relevant to the review question. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task contrast / parametric modulation related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet. Exclusion criteria met: none. Final decision: EXCLUDED due to lack of relevance to reward cue-reactivity (study does not examine drug/natural reward visual cues).

This study does not meet the review’s task-type inclusion requirements. Although it is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with group-level voxelwise analyses reported (I6) and whole-brain results described in the text/tables (I7), it used a probabilistic reversal-learning reward task and contrasts such as negative > positive feedback, final reversal > reversal error, and final reversal error > correct responses. These contrasts do not correspond to the risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts specified by the inclusion criteria (I4 and I5), nor does the study examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual cues targeted by the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (estimating a briefly flashed stimulus location) and includes within-task contrasts comparing conditions (e.g., individual information alone vs integration conditions I:I, I:S, S:S). Imaging was analyzed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak MNI coordinates. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps relevant to perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choice between risky £1 vs safer 10p options) during fMRI under ketamine and placebo. The paper reports within-task computationally derived contrasts related to risk-related decision variables (choice temperature, learning rate; outcome confirmatory vs contradictory), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and paired t-tests) and reports results in text/figures/ROIs. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/decision variables), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a card gambling task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (decision-phase regressors for six risk levels; outcome contrasts grouped by risk level; risk magnitude linear effects) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and stereotactic coordinates reported. Results and contrasts relevant to risk (e.g., risk level effects, low-risk vs high-risk negative outcomes, risk-related linear increase in VS) are described in the text and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical).

The study used fMRI and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6 satisfied) and presents results in text/figures (I7 satisfied). However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task: participants passively viewed stimulus sequences and provided post-hoc causal ratings rather than making in-task risky/ambiguous/perceptual choices, and no within-task contrasts of the form 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguity', or 'hard > easy' are reported. Therefore it fails I4 and I5 and does not meet the review’s task-specific inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli: this paper investigates decoding of near-threshold pain perception using laser somatosensory stimulation and multivariate analyses, not reward cue-reactivity or visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making task: subjects judged painful vs non-painful), I5 (within-task contrasts/decoding for perceptual decisions such as pain vs no-pain/anticipation vs stimulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses and voxelwise maps reported), I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (none of I4–I7 are unmet). Exclusion criteria met: [] (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (core article content present: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study used fMRI of probabilistic association learning (Weather Prediction Task) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy), nor does it address reward-related cue-reactivity with visual stimuli which is the meta-analysis objective. Therefore it fails to meet I4 and I5 despite providing whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

Although this paper is an fMRI study of risky decision-making that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and task contrasts, it does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task/between-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with coordinates/parametric maps). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Primary reason for exclusion: topic mismatch — the study investigates monetary risky choices and conflict monitoring, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual stimuli, so it does not address the review objective.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s task domain criteria. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported and voxel-wise t-tests with cluster correction are described) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported in text/figures). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (the fMRI task is the Monetary Incentive Delay task, which measures reward anticipation/receipt and simple reaction-time responding, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguity”, or “hard>easy” are reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study is an fMRI investigation of perceptual decision-making (dot-motion coherence) with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reported task contrasts; it therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (no reward or cue-reactivity paradigm, no substance/natural reward stimuli or related contrasts). None of the exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply (the study reports whole-brain results, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is empirical). Because the study does not address the review topic (reward cue-reactivity), it must be excluded.

Although this study meets the technical fMRI decision-making criteria (I4–I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis review objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task), I5 (within-task contrast: decision-making > control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: the study does not examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues (the primary review topic), so it is ineligible for this reward-cue meta-analysis despite meeting I4–I7. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

Although the study involves perceptual decision-making tasks performed in MRI sessions (Experiments 1–3 include MRI/mock-MRI sessions), the full text presents behavioral analyses and LBA modeling only and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked fMRI activation maps or task contrasts (e.g., hard>easy) required for inclusion. Therefore: inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI session with perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported within- or between-task fMRI contrasts in this paper), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly triggered by the content provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks the required whole-brain fMRI activation/contrast data.

Although this paper reports empirical fMRI data with a risky/uncertain decision-making task and whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (meets I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not address the meta-analysis objective: drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual reward cues. The study investigates probability learning and decision-making for monetary payoffs rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not relevant to the review's topic and is excluded on that basis. Full text is complete.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI inclusion criteria (see below), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Specifically, this is an fMRI study of attentional deployment and regret in a sequential risk-taking task with monetary/gold outcomes, not a cue-reactivity study of drug or natural rewards. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk: Opt vs Nopt, GF vs MF, etc.), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Because the study does not address the review objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity), it is excluded.

Although this fMRI study used perceptual/ambiguous target-detection and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (meeting I4–I7), it does not address the review’s topical objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The task involves visual target/distractor morphs and attentional/ambiguity contrasts rather than reward-cue reactivity or drug/natural reward stimuli. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this reward cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI but during a working-memory (n-back) task, not while participants performed a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (IGT). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the 2-back>0-back contrast) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making was reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an event-related, whole-brain fMRI study of human decision-making (Iowa Gambling Task) and meets the methodological fMRI inclusion criteria, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Specifically: the task involves monetary decision-making under uncertainty (IGT), not cue-reactivity paradigms featuring drug or natural reward cues (visual). Therefore it is not relevant to the review question and must be excluded. The paper does perform whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports task contrasts (anticipation vs experience; gain/draw/loss; deck contrasts), but the population and task are outside the scope of reward cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply.

This study acquired task-based fMRI during a gambling decision-making task with explicit high-uncertainty (Lose) vs low-uncertainty (Win) conditions, providing within-task contrasts (Lose vs Win). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses were conducted with SPM8 (reported task condition main effects and coordinates/tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Results and contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity/resting-state, and is empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice task (face vs house) manipulating stimulus difficulty (phase coherence). It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard > easy; low coherence > high coherence) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected) with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Results and contrasts are described in the text and tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI in healthy adults). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI inclusion criteria (I4–I7: it used an fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making task (IGT), reports within-task contrasts (e.g., risky > safe, anticipation, win > loss), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported in text/tables/figures), it does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. This study examines monetary reward-based decision-making and neural responses during the IGT rather than visual cue-reactivity to drugs/natural rewards. Therefore it is excluded for not matching the review’s topical objective. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain task maps and within-task contrasts of decision-making under uncertainty, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective. The paper reports a 4-arm bandit decision-making task probing exploration/exploitation and model-based uncertainty, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual cues. Therefore it is not relevant to a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward visual stimuli and must be excluded.

Although this study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results during a reward-guided decision-making (probabilistic reversal) task and provides voxelwise maps (meets I4, I6, I7), it does not report any within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly targeting risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Reported contrasts focus on reward vs. punishment and model-derived prediction-error parametric effects, not on risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty contrasts required by I5. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implemented a risky decision-making (roulette) task contrasting low- vs high-probability (risky vs safe) and gain vs loss conditions. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., high vs low probability, gain > loss) and group-level analyses. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results are described (whole-brain analyses and Supplementary Tables of activated foci are referenced), in addition to ROI analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text unavailable (fulltext_incomplete=true). Title indicates an fMRI study of decision-making under risk in Parkinson's disease, but the provided content is 'nan' so I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) — not confirmed; I5 (within- or between-task contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) — not confirmed; I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) — not confirmed; I7 (whole-brain results reported/clearly described) — not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied based on the available metadata. Excluding because essential inclusion criteria cannot be verified due to incomplete full text.

The paper reports simultaneous EEG-fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning reward-learning task and provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate tables (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is a reward-learning paradigm rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified in I4, and the reported contrasts focus on outcome valence and unsigned prediction error (surprise) rather than contrasts explicitly comparing risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty conditions required by I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5 are not met) and is excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and reports results primarily using ROI-constrained analyses (Exclusion E3). It does include an fMRI task involving probabilistic reversal learning (meets I4: task-based fMRI) and includes within-task contrasts related to adaptive behaviour after feedback (meets I5). However, it does NOT meet I6 (no unmasked whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; results were SVC within pre-specified ROIs) and I7 (no acceptable whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Additionally, the study topic (probabilistic reversal learning in anorexia nervosa) does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward visual stimuli. Full text appears complete.

The study performed task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), modeling contrasts that index choice under high uncertainty (shift>stay) and outcome processing (reward>punishment). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TFCE-corrected across the whole brain) and provides coordinates/figures for significant clusters. Thus: I4 (fMRI during ambiguous/uncertain decision-making) is satisfied; I5 (within-task contrasts related to ambiguous/risky decision-making—shift>stay reflects choice under uncertainty) is satisfied; I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps) is satisfied; I7 (results reported as coordinates/figures/text) is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it meets several technical inclusion criteria for fMRI decision-making studies — I4: yes (group fMRI while participants performed a risky lottery decision-making task); I5: yes (within-task parametric contrasts related to risk, e.g., ΔMin, ΔEV, and ΔU; PPI analyses and task-related modulatory contrasts are reported); I6: yes (group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported and whole-brain activations are summarized in tables); I7: yes (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, it fails the review’s topical requirement: it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues, but instead examines cognitive/affective processes in risky decision making for self vs others. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore excluded because the study does not address the review objective (cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) with manipulations of expected value, uncertainty, and urgency. It reports within-task contrasts related to risk/EV (e.g., positive EV > negative EV, neutral vs. negative/positive) and interactions with urgency. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are described (SPM8; voxel-level p<0.001 with cluster-level correction) and whole-brain results are reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet the key task-related inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. While it reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (I6) and clearly describes whole-brain results/figures (I7), the experimental paradigm is a reinforcement-learning/probabilistic gain-loss learning task (reward vs. punishment prediction error encoding), not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (a within-task or between-task contrast directly related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because required inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

This fMRI study involved human participants performing a risky decision-making task (a virtual sexual ‘hook up’ game) and reports task contrasts (SRD > implicit baseline; SRD > conversational) and between-group contrasts (Risky > Safe), satisfying inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, the neuroimaging analyses were conducted and reported within predefined anatomical/functional ROIs (TFCE contrasts within four decision-making ROIs and ROI-based follow-ups). Although some covariate analyses were run at the whole-brain level with null results, the primary reported task-evoked group contrasts and cluster results are ROI-restricted and not presented as unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). This places it within exclusion criterion E3 (reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain task map). I7 is not applicable because the required whole-brain task maps are not reported. Full text appears complete.

Although the full text reports a group-level, whole-brain fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty (Shannon entropy) and provides task contrasts and PPI connectivity, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. The task involved monetary choice between delayed/probabilistic rewards (economic decisions), not presentation of drug or natural reward cues or visual cue-reactivity contrasts. Therefore the study is not relevant to the review topic and is excluded on that basis.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI decision-making inclusion criteria (see below), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective. The review seeks fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cue-reactivity). This study examines adolescent risk processing during an economic lottery decision-making task (monetary gambles) and cognitive control (MSIT), not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. Therefore it is not conceptually eligible for a meta-analysis of reward cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task - lottery choice), I5 (within-task contrast related to risk: high vs low CV), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analysis reported), I7 (results/coordinates reported in text/appendices). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because it does not address reward cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues required by the meta-analysis objective.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not address the review objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results described in text/supplement). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the in-scanner task is a monetary card-guessing reward expectancy paradigm rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task focused on drug/natural reward cues) and I5 (no within-task contrast explicitly framed as risky>safe or analogous risk/ambiguity contrast using drug/natural reward cues). Because the primary meta-analysis objective requires studies of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, this monetary reward task does not meet the review objective despite having whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this is an empirical human fMRI study of decision-making with group-level whole-brain task maps and within-task contrasts, it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experiment involves a monetary limited-offer sequential decision task (risky choice/planning) rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues. Therefore, despite satisfying the fMRI/task-related inclusion criteria, it is not relevant to the review topic and must be excluded.

The full text is a complete empirical fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (cognitive flexibility) with whole-brain group analyses and reported coordinates. It does NOT meet the review’s decision-making task requirements: (1) I4 not met — the task is a probabilistic reversal learning task focused on reward prediction errors/cognitive flexibility, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the inclusion examples; (2) I5 not met — no within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) are reported — the main contrasts are parametric RPE effects and group comparisons of RPE processing. It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effects reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Exclusion rationale: Although this is an empirical fMRI study with a risky decision-making task, whole-brain group analyses, and reported contrasts, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6 apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: stock vs. bond, risky>safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (results/tables/contrast files provided in supplements). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: While I4–I7 are satisfied, the study does not examine visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards and therefore is not relevant to the review objective. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE due to lack of topical relevance to the review question (not a cue-reactivity visual-stimuli study).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based risky decision-making fMRI. It acquired task-based fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) (I4). The authors modeled risk-level (Pumps) and produced within-task, risk-related contrasts/parametric maps (risk level-related activation) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported (one-sample t-test with cluster-level FWE correction; risk-level z-statistic maps) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6) and results are described in the text/figures/tables (I7). The paper also contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E3), not solely resting-state/seed connectivity (E4) — although resting-state analyses are included, they do not replace the task activation maps — and it is an empirical fMRI study with within-task effects (not E5 or E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study should be excluded. It does involve fMRI during a probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making task (meets I4) and reports within-task comparisons between task stages (meets I5). However, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise results: analyses are ROI-based and multivariate within predefined ROIs, and the main reported results are ROI/multivariate statistics and selected-voxel maps rather than unmasked whole-brain activation maps. Therefore I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met and Exclusion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving game) in the scanner, with explicit within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe decisions (Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Pass > Crash). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 models with voxelwise FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus it meets I4 (task-based risky decision-making fMRI), I5 (risky>safe contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While the study is an empirical, whole-brain task fMRI investigation of risky decision making and meets the listed imaging inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The task uses probabilistic deck choices with numeric stimuli and models risk prediction, not visual cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore, despite satisfying I4–I7, the study is not relevant to the review objective and is excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in human participants using the risky-gains task (a risky decision-making paradigm). The authors report a within-task contrast of interest (risky > safe) and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 t-maps) with reported thresholds, clusters, figures and tables. ROI analyses are also present but whole-brain results are reported, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only effects, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling appraisal. Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain risky decision-making contrasts.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that explicitly manipulated ambiguity in a decision-making task (ambiguous vs. generalization contexts) and used trial-wise model-based contrasts (Shannon entropy of prior belief) tied to ambiguity. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE-corrected activations (including hippocampus, amygdala, fusiform, precuneus) and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described and illustrated. Thus it meets I4 (human fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (ambiguity-related within-task parametric contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (model-free prediction errors and model-based minus model-free prediction error contrasts), it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required. The task is a sequential model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning paradigm focused on reward prediction errors and the balance of control, not contrasts such as ‘risky > safe’, ‘ambiguity > non-ambiguous’, or perceptual difficulty contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one within-task or between-task contrast mapped to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) are not met. Inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are met (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported and acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of statistical learning and prediction using structured vs random symbol sequences. While it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (meets I6) and presents whole-brain results in text/figures (meets I7), it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (participants performed prediction/statistical-learning tasks, not risky/uncertain choice or perceptual difficulty contrasts). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines social decision-making in the Ultimatum Game (unfair vs fair offers; decision to accept/reject) in healthy women. While it reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I6) and presents results in tables/figures (I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required (I4 not met) and does not include within-task contrasts matching the risk/ambiguity/perceptual examples (I5 not met). Additionally, the study does not address drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli (outside the review objective). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply and the full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of truth-telling and risk propensity using a social Communication Game, not a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli. Although it collected whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6) and reports results in text/tables/figures (I7), and involved an fMRI decision-making task under asymmetric information (I4), it does not include a within-task contrast of the type required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (I5) nor any cue-reactivity contrasts (e.g., drug cue > neutral cue). Therefore it does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

This study does not address the review objective (reward-related cue-reactivity) and fails to meet required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI task is a prediction/statistical-learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty are reported), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast maps appropriate for meta-analysis of cue-reactivity are provided). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are specifically met (the paper reports whole-brain ICA-derived component maps and network analyses but these are not the voxelwise task contrasts required). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the primary task-domain inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (the paper reports whole-brain, cross-subject offline whole-brain classification and reports discriminating volumes/voxel-wise weights) and I7 (whole-brain results are described in the text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is the social economic ultimatum game, which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and I5 (no within-task contrast framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as “risky>safe” or “high uncertainty>low uncertainty” is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I4: the fMRI scans were conducted during passive free-viewing of faces and an emotion regulation (reappraise vs maintain) task, not during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. It does include contrasts comparing ambiguous (surprised) versus neutral faces (Surprise>Neutral), satisfying I5, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (with cluster correction), satisfying I6 and acceptable reporting per I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because I4 is not met (fMRI task is not a decision-making paradigm), despite meeting I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of text-based recalibration of speech perception (auditory perceptual decision-making). While it meets methodological inclusion criteria I4 (perceptual decision-making task: /aba/ vs /ada/ categorization), I5 (task-related contrasts/post-test trials), I6 (group-level whole-brain RFX GLM maps corrected for multiple comparisons), and I7 (results reported as whole-brain maps/figures), it does NOT address the review’s topical objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study investigates audiovisual language/reading effects, not reward cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore excluded due to topic mismatch (does not address reward cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing the Salience Attribution Test, a task with probabilistic (uncertain) reward cues and speeded responses. The authors report within-task contrasts that compare high- vs low-probability reward cue features (adaptive reward prediction) and contrasts probing cues with identical (ambiguous/uncertain 50%) reward probabilities (aberrant reward prediction). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are performed and whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates), with supplementary VOI/SVC analyses; results are described in detail in the text and coordinates are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies I4 (fMRI during a task involving uncertainty/ambiguous reward cues), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing high vs low probability / ambiguous cues), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (coordinates and whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Exclusion(s) met: E3 (study reports primarily ROI-focused analyses without reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion(s) met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/perceptual decision-making task — land vs. do-not-land trials), I5 (within-task contrasts modeled: decision trials vs. control; correct vs. incorrect). Inclusion(s) not met: I6 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map or unmasked whole-brain task effect presented), I7 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplementary materials). The full text is complete. Because the paper reports ROI-constrained analyses and does not present unmasked whole-brain task-evoked maps or coordinates required for inclusion, it must be excluded under E3.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity to visual cues) and does not report the requisite decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is a social/advice-based hierarchical learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review) and I5 (no within-task contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g., “risky > safe” or “ambiguous > non-ambiguous” — instead results focus on model-based prediction-error regressors). Exclusion criteria: none applicable (E3–E6 not met). Full text is complete for screening purposes.
