Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps reported (meets I6 and I7), it does NOT meet the critical design requirement I4: scanning was performed during a Pavlovian conditioning/imperative task in which participants passively viewed cues and pressed a location button, rather than performing a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Consequently the key inclusion contrast requirement I5 is not satisfied: the reported contrasts probe parametric stimulus-related signals (expected value, variance/uncertainty) during cue presentation rather than within-task or between-task decision contrasts such as “risky > safe” or “high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty” derived from participants making choices. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) in schizophrenia that reports whole-brain task-evoked results. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards using visual stimuli, nor does it implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task with contrasts such as "risky > safe" or "ambiguity > non-ambiguous." It satisfies I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures), but fails I4 (task type) and I5 (required contrast types). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a Selection task involving choices between two simultaneously presented risky lotteries (risk defined as variance). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk and choice (e.g., choosing riskier > surer; contrasts for ∑Var, ΔVar, Var_chosen > Var_unchosen, chosen vs unchosen EV/SV), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides peak coordinates and tables. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risk-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by inclusion criteria. It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked fMRI analyses (meets I6) and reports whole-brain results in the text (meets I7). However, it does NOT meet I4 (task is a visuomotor finger-tapping task with chosen vs specified actions, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and does NOT meet I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not address the review objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli). It used olfactory conditioned stimuli and monetary reward in an associative learning paradigm, not visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria: I4 is met (fMRI during a perceptual odour-detection task). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported within-task univariate contrast framed as perceptual decision-making contrasts such as “hard>easy” or perceptual task>control), I6 (no standard group-level, whole-brain task-evoked univariate activation map reported for a perceptual contrast), I7 (not applicable because I6 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Therefore the paper fails to satisfy required inclusion criteria and is not eligible for the meta-analysis.

The study investigates neural processing of vocal prosody and social communicative intentions using an fMRI classification task with auditory stimuli. It does not address drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and does not implement a risky, reward-related, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (it is a prosody classification/categorization task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported) and I7 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task in the review sense) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents that used a risky decision-making task (modified Jackpot task with play vs pass decisions under varied risk/stake levels), reported task-related contrasts (e.g., Play > Pass; Social Play vs Monetary Play; Gain > Pass) and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected clusters and peak coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, participants, fMRI acquisition/analyses), Results (whole-brain and ROI results), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making) with adolescents. It reports a risky > safe contrast and conducts group-level, voxelwise SPM8 analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) with whole-brain results and coordinates for activations and brain–behavior correlations. Results are reported as voxel coordinates and statistical maps (with thresholding and cluster correction). Thus the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI: I4 (task: Risky-Gains), I5 (risky > safe contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task whole-brain effects, empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). It is an empirical fMRI study of risky/loss decision-making in depressed patients and suicide attempters. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making tasks), I5 (task-related contrasts/regressors related to risk/loss), I6 (group-level whole-brain/random-effects analyses reported, with ROI and exploratory whole-brain results), I7 (whole-brain results described in text and supplementary tables). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 — they are satisfied — but the study fails to match the review topic (reward cue-reactivity to drug/natural cues with visual stimuli), so it is not relevant for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study does not address the review objective (fMRI of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity) and does not involve participants performing a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Participants passively viewed magic, causal-control, and surprise video clips; no contrasts of risky>safe, ambiguity>control, or hard>easy perceptual decisions are reported. However, the study does report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and provides coordinates/tables (fulfilling I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6). Therefore the paper must be excluded because inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

Excluded because the study does not address the meta-analysis objective: it investigates neural encoding of variance and skewness in risky decision-making, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/choice reported, e.g., variance/skewness and gamble>sure), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported with FWE-corrected clusters), I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Therefore excluded on topical grounds (does not match review objective). Full text appears complete.

This study investigates classifier performance (GNB, SVM, LDA) in multi-subject searchlight fMRI analyses of speech/phoneme categorization (/ba/ vs /da/). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight random-effects maps) and I7 (whole-brain results presented in figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is phoneme perception, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined for the review) and I5 (no contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not relevant to the meta-analysis objective and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analogue Risk Task) during scanning. The paper models risk decisions (pump events) in a whole-brain, group-level GLM and reports group-level whole-brain results (deactivation in DMN and activation in task-active regions) in figures/tables; unthresholded individual maps/parameter estimates were also extracted from whole-brain maps. Behavioral contrasts and within-task effects related to risk decisions are explicitly modeled and used in analyses. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk decisions), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables described in text). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (whole-brain results are reported), not resting-state/seed-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study includes an in-scanner risky decision-making task (Balloon Analogue Risk Task), modeling parametric risk levels (1–9) and extracting BOLD responses—meeting I4. It reports within-task contrasts related to risk level and group comparisons (parametric modulation and average risk-level activations), fulfilling I5. The manuscript describes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses of BOLD activation associated with risk level and reports whole-brain activation patterns and comparisons, satisfying I6. Results are reported in-text and with figures/ROIs and whole-brain findings, consistent with I7. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task and imaging analysis), Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the paper does not report only ROI or connectivity/resting analyses, and it presents whole-brain task activation maps at the group level. Therefore the study should be included.

The study does not address reward-related cue-reactivity or decision-making tasks required by the review. It used an n-back working memory task (0-back vs 2-back) in schizophrenia patients, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. It therefore fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, it does provide group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (baseline vs 2-back), satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports primarily ROI-focused analyses with Small Volume Correction and does not present or report unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps or whole-brain corrected results. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk, e.g., gamble > certain, risky > non-risky). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), which leads to exclusion under E3. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports fMRI of humans performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts and group-by-decision contrasts (risky vs safe and related contrasts), satisfying I5. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted using AFNI with cluster correction and reported Talairach coordinates and cluster results, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/coordinates) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and provides whole-brain task activation maps rather than only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI activation maps related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task — time perception task was behavioral and fMRI was resting-state), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty), I6 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I7 (not applicable because no task-based whole-brain results are presented). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's decision-making task inclusion criteria. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are described in the text/figures). Not met: I4 (the fMRI task is a passive cue-reactivity picture-viewing task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans with whole-brain group-level analyses, but does not contain contrasts of risky vs safe, ambiguous vs unambiguous, or perceptual difficulty contrasts required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is a gambling/outcome task but not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined) and I5 (no within-task contrasts indexing risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty; contrasts are outcome-based: wins vs non-wins, near-miss vs full-miss, and an interaction with choice). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (e.g., the paper is not ROI-only nor solely connectivity-only; whole-brain GLM results are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded because it fails to meet I4 and I5.

This fMRI study investigates visual food-cue reactivity (Food > Non-Food) and reports group-level analyses. However it does not test a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as required (no contrasts like hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or other perceptual-DM contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were generated and reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are described and available in the Supplementary material). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E6) are triggered by the available full text. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet the mandatory decision-making task-related inclusion criteria I4 and I5.
